thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: NETWORK ALERT — unusual packet loss and route churn detected
incident-bot: Sources: telemetry, BGP watcher, edge-pop-health. Affected prefixes: 3.120.64.0/18, 3.120.128.0/18 (us-east-facing mesh). Observed loss > 25% between our egress via AS65010 (provider-zenith) and edge POPs.
sara: paging @matt (oncall) — looks like provider-zenith interconnect issues. see netops feed.
matt: I'm awake, looking. oncall now. can someone post the BGP dump and traceroute?
netops-bot: BGP flaps logged:
```
Prefix: 3.120.64.0/18
Announcements: via AS65010 -> AS64500 (flap count 27 in 10m)
AS path variations: 65010 64500 64520 ... 64520 65010
```
lee: traceroute from egress (us-east-1) to edge-pop-nyc shows asymmetry, next hop changes and then blackholing at hop 6
```
traceroute to 3.120.64.12
1 10.0.0.1
2 198.51.100.5
3 203.0.113.9 (provider-zenith)
4 203.0.113.25 (AS64500)
5 * * *
6 * * *  <-- loss here
```
chloe: confirmed from our monitoring: p50 latency spikes to 800ms and p95 > 2s for requests served via the affected egress. Dedicated customers show increased error rates for long-tail flows.
sara: quick customer impact summary for status page: "Partial network degradation affecting traffic between our US and EU regions via provider-zenith. Some API calls may experience high latency or packet loss. Engineers are investigating." Should I post?
ana: (typo) sorry meant ana: I'll draft and post. tagging support for customer comms.
nana: (deleted)
nana: (ignore)
support: pushing to status page now — setting to Investigating.
statusbot: Status page updated: INCIDENT-#0123 Investigating — Network degradation between regions.
matt: mitigation plan: 1) validate alternate provider (AS65020) path 2) announce more specific /24s to steer away from provider-zenith 3) contact provider-zenith to escalate ticket 4) monitor.
lee: I can prep the more specifics. recommend `announce /24s` for the two /18s temporarily. Also try BGP prepend removal on AS65010 to prefer AS65020.
chloe: we can do a gradual shift — avoid full withdraw. do a weighted egress change on our load balancer/wrapping fabric.
sara: command ready for netops team. matt, can you authorize emergency more-specific announcement?
matt: authorize. do it in 2-step: announce, wait 5m, validate, then scale.
chloe: applying announcement now via exabgp on border-2:
```
# exabgp announce sample
announce route 3.120.64.0/24 next-hop 198.51.100.2 community 65020:100
announce route 3.120.128.0/24 next-hop 198.51.100.2 community 65020:100
```
chloe: announce done. watchers, please eyeball BGP table and telemetry.
netops-bot: New announcements seen via AS65020. Route propagation to peers in 2m.
lee: traceroute after announce shows path now via AS65020 and no blackholing, packet loss down to 1-2%
```
traceroute to 3.120.64.12
1 10.0.0.1
2 198.51.101.9
3 198.51.101.14 (provider-alt AS65020)
4 198.51.101.22
5 203.0.113.100
6 3.120.64.12
```
chloe: perf numbers improving: p50 back to 60ms, p95 ~180ms. errors trending down.
ama: support: doing a batch message to top 20 impacted customers, flagging for potential retry logic.
sara: great. escalate to provider-zenith support: ticket #Z-87921 opened, engineer assigned, asked about route leak/peer config.
matt: calling out action items for incident: Coordinator: matt; NetOps: chloe/lee; Customer comms: ana; Contact provider: sara; Monitoring: add watch rule for rapid route churn.
lee: oncall notes: seems like a route leak or misconfigured upstream causing AS64500 to reannounce our prefixes through the wrong path. full RCA will need provider logs.
matt: quick mitigation success — traffic shifted to AS65020, telemetry stable. keeping incident live while we watch for reverts.
incident-bot: Page logs: 3 pages, 2 oncall acknowledgements.
sara: update to status page — Investigating -> Partial Service Interruption. Including note: "Traffic being rerouted to alternate backbone; mitigation in progress." Posting now.
statusbot: Status page updated: INCIDENT-#0123 Partial Service Interruption.
nana: (again meant ana) support: customers notified, engineering notes included.
matt: handing off to night oncall @lee in 45m. Lee — accept and I'll write a brief handoff.
lee: accepted. please include current checkpoints and watchlist.
matt: handoff checklist:
- Monitor BGP flaps for prefixes 3.120.64.0/18 & 3.120.128.0/18
- Keep provider-zenith ticket open, escalate every 30m until they confirm fix
- Don't withdraw /24s until provider gives clean BGP state for 20m
- Post any customer-impact changes to status page
- Runbook link: /runbooks/network/egress-route-leak (temp doc)
lee: got it. I'll keep 30m polling and will escalate if flaps return.
chloe: pushing a short-term monitor tweak to alert at 5% loss for these prefixes.
netops-bot: Alert rules updated.
matt: quick check: can we capture full MRTBGP dump for provider handoff? we need history.
chloe: saving MRT dumps, shipping to provider-zenith ticket and to S3 (s3://redwood-incidents/INC-0123/mrtbgs/).
nana: (ana) support: logging top customer cases and owners.
sara: ~30m after mitigation, metrics stable. keeping incident open for postmortem items.
incident-bot: INCIDENT-#0123 status: mitigation applied.
matt: declared mitigation successful. leaving follow-ups: 1) RCA with provider log correlation, 2) improve automatic failover runbook, 3) add BGP community-based pref steering to test harness.
nana: support to follow up with impacted customers with detailed timeline once RCA is available.
lee: closing notes: root cause initial hypothesis — upstream route leak from AS64500 causing traffic to traverse provider-zenith and get blackholed intermittently. vendor-induced route churn. final confirmation pending vendor logs.
chloe: PR for automations queued: add-step to automatically announce /24s for critical egress on detected >15% loss and flap count >10 in 10m (safety gating included).
sara: thanks all. will schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00am PT.
statusbot: Status page updated: INCIDENT-#0123 Monitoring.
matt: incident resolved (mitigated) handoff complete. moving to post-incident actions. :white_check_mark:
